scope: Core technical vocabulary for Color: Linux/Bash, source code, data, Git, runtime, network, delivery, security and observability. Not an exhaustive dictionary of computing; no colors or new runtime roles are assigned.

fields.role: Stable rendering identifier; references a concept but need not use its exact singular spelling.
fields.category: Functional grouping of a role; separate from structural relationships.
fields.color_code: Legacy symbolic color identifier; not a concept or authoritative hex value.
fields.hex_value: Foreground RGB representation, separate from the vocabulary.
fields.hierarchy: Existing mixed classification label; not an explicit parent-child edge.
fields.source_type: Whether a role was shipped (static) or registered (dynamic); not execution behavior.
fields.app_linked: Application or context associated with a role.
fields.install_hook: Legacy hook identifier; not proof a function or hook executes.

legacy_hierarchies.parent: Existing Color label for primary containers or interface anchors; not a universal parent relationship.
legacy_hierarchies.child: Existing Color label for subordinate storage objects; the actual containing object is context-dependent.
legacy_hierarchies.cousin: Existing Color label for related, functionally distinct objects; not literal filesystem ancestry.
legacy_hierarchies.alert: Existing Color label for attention-requiring conditions.
legacy_hierarchies.feedback: Existing Color label for reported outcomes.
legacy_hierarchies.language: Existing Color label for programming language identity.
legacy_hierarchies.runtime: Existing Color label for an execution environment.

relation_types.contains: May include an instance of another concept; not mandatory containment.
relation_types.references: Points to or identifies another concept.
relation_types.accepts: May take this kind of input.
relation_types.declares: Defines a named constituent in its own specification.

terms.definition: Organized storage and naming system for files.
Container mapping names to filesystem entries.
In this Color vocabulary, a regular filesystem object storing bytes. Linux also uses file in a broader sense covering directories and special objects.
Filesystem entry containing a target pathname.
Directory entry referring to an existing filesystem inode; every hard link to the object refers to the same inode.
Filesystem record identifying an object and its metadata.
Name or sequence of names used to locate a filesystem object.
Path starting at the filesystem root.
Path interpreted relative to a starting directory.
Attachment of a filesystem at a path in the directory hierarchy.
Process-local integer handle for an open resource.
Named pipe through which processes can exchange bytes.
Allowed access to an object, such as reading, writing or executing.
User identity associated with a filesystem object.
Collection of user identities used in access decisions.
In this filesystem vocabulary, a file with execute permission; the permission does not guarantee that execution will succeed.
Single representation containing multiple stored files or entries.
Encoding data to use fewer bytes where possible.
Computed value used to detect changes or corruption.
Independent recoverable copy of data or configuration.
Stored reusable result that avoids repeating work.
Interface that sends input to and displays output from programs.
Program that interprets commands and manages their execution.
Displayed indication that the shell is ready for input.
Invocation of a program, builtin or function.
Command implemented by the shell itself.
Shell substitution for a command word.
Argument interpreted as a modifier of command behavior.
Value or expression supplied at a command or function invocation.
File containing instructions intended for an interpreter.
Leading interpreter directive in a Unix executable text file.
Named value in a process environment; in Bash, exported shell variables are passed to child processes.
Conventional input stream, normally descriptor 0.
Conventional normal-output stream, normally descriptor 1.
Conventional diagnostic stream, normally descriptor 2.
Connection carrying output of one command into input of another.
Shell operation connecting an input or output descriptor to a different destination.
Redirection supplying a block of text as input until a delimiter.
Expansion inserting a command's captured output.
Shell substitution or transformation of a parameter's value.
Filename pattern expanded by the shell.
Syntax controlling how shell characters are interpreted.
Numeric completion result of a command.
Separate shell execution environment derived from the calling shell.
Shell-managed command or pipeline, possibly in the background.
Notification delivered to a process or thread.
Running instance of a program with its own execution context.
Numeric process identifier.
Execution path within a process sharing process resources.
Formal notation for expressing computation.
Language extending JavaScript with static type syntax.
Programming language standardized as ECMAScript.
Name used to refer to a declared or accessible program entity.
Named binding whose value can be used in a program.
In JavaScript and TypeScript, a binding declared with const cannot be reassigned; referenced object contents may still change.
Source notation directly expressing a value.
Data represented or manipulated by a program.
Classification describing allowable values or operations.
Sequence of textual units.
Numeric value; representation depends on the language.
Logical value of true or false.
Explicit representation of no value in languages that provide it.
JavaScript value typically indicating no assigned or provided value.
Indexed collection of elements.
JavaScript entity holding properties; other languages define objects differently.
Named member of an object.
Identifier used to access an entry in a mapping.
Code that evaluates to a value.
Syntactic instruction in a program.
Syntax denoting an operation on operands.
Operation setting a binding or storage location to a value.
Syntax introducing a binding or named program entity.
Callable block of behavior that can accept inputs and produce a result.
Named input declared by a function; it receives a supplied argument or a default where applicable.
Value produced by a function call.
Region in which a binding can be accessed.
Function retaining access to its surrounding lexical bindings.
Expression evaluated to choose behavior.
Selecting one execution path from alternatives.
Control structure repeating work.
Raised condition that transfers control to error handling.
Definition used to describe or construct objects.
Object created from a class or other constructor.
Function associated with an object or class.
In TypeScript, a declaration naming an object or callable type's shape.
Name assigned to a TypeScript type expression.
Type or function parameterized over one or more types.
Unit of code with its own boundary and potentially imports or exports.
Declaration or operation making another module's exports accessible.
Declaration exposing a binding from a module.
Source text intended for readers rather than execution.
Pattern language for matching text.
JavaScript object representing an eventual operation result or rejection.
Function whose invocation returns a promise in JavaScript.
Syntax waiting for a promise's settlement within an appropriate async context.
Tool translating source into another representation.
Program executing instructions expressed in a source or intermediate language.
Rules governing the structure of valid source text.
Meaning or behavior of a syntactically valid construct.
Text format for representing structured data.
Text serialization format frequently used for configuration.
Description of the expected structure and constraints of data, such as a JSON document.
Checking data or behavior against specified rules.
Rule restricting permitted values or relationships.
Organized data store managed for retrieval and modification.
Relational structure organizing data in rows and columns.
One set of column values in a table.
Named attribute of a table with a declared data type.
Database constraint that identifies each row uniquely using one or more non-null columns.
Constraint linking values to a referenced unique or primary key.
Data structure supporting efficient lookup or other database operations.
Request to retrieve or manipulate data.
Unit of database work that commits or rolls back as a group.
Make a database transaction's changes permanent according to database guarantees.
In SQL, abort the current transaction and discard its uncommitted changes.
Controlled change to a database schema or other versioned data format.
Named database query presented as a relation.
Operation combining rows from relations using a matching condition.
Database copy maintained from another database.
Reusable set of database connections.
Mechanism restricting concurrent access to a resource.
Cycle of waiting operations that prevents progress without intervention.
terms.example: two transactions waiting on each other

terms.definition: Encoding data into a representation suitable for storage or transfer.
Whether a field or type permits a null value.
Named namespace within a PostgreSQL database that organizes tables and other database objects.
Git object database and references, with optional working tree.
Checked-out files plus local changes.
Git data structure holding staged content and related metadata for the next commit; also holds conflict stages during a merge.
Git object recording a tree, parent links and metadata.
Line of Git development whose tip is tracked by a movable reference to a commit.
In Git, a name that identifies an object directly or through another reference.
Git HEAD identifies the current branch or a directly checked-out commit in detached HEAD state.
Git reference under refs/tags identifying an object, often used to mark a release; unlike a branch it does not advance automatically when commits are made.
Named configuration for another repository location.
Create a local repository from another repository.
Download remote Git objects and update configured tracking references.
Fetch followed by integration into the current branch.
Send objects and request updates to remote references.
Integrate histories, often creating a commit with multiple parents.
Replay commits onto a different base, usually changing their identities.
Representation of differences between two states.
Incompatible changes requiring resolution before integration can finish.
Proposal to review and integrate changes between branches on a hosting platform.
Inspection of proposed changes for correctness and suitability.
Object identifier for a particular Git commit.
Saved working-tree and index changes that can be reapplied.
Populate or switch checked-out content from a Git reference or path.
Apply changes introduced by a selected commit to another history.
Create a new commit reversing changes from an earlier commit.
Stored Git entity of type blob, tree, commit or annotated tag.
Execution environment providing facilities needed by a program.
JavaScript runtime built around V8 and system APIs.
Core operating-system component managing hardware and process resources.
System software managing resources and providing an execution environment.
Machine or environment providing resources to another workload.
Software-defined computer running a guest operating system.
Read-only template containing filesystem layers and configuration for creating Docker containers.
Runnable instance created from a container image; when running, its processes execute with isolation.
Instruction file describing how Docker builds an image.
Filesystem changeset contributing to a container image.
Docker-managed storage that can persist beyond a container lifecycle.
Mount exposing a file or directory from the Docker daemon host at a path in a container.
Service storing and distributing container images.
Managed capability or workload made available to consumers.
Background process providing ongoing functionality.
Execution component consuming work from a queue or scheduler.
Component selecting when or where work runs.
Time-based trigger for work or another unit.
Resource managed by systemd, such as a service or timer.
Distribution unit containing software and metadata.
Component required by another component to build or run.
Recorded resolved dependency versions and associated metadata.
Structured declaration of a package or workload's metadata and requirements.
Settings determining system behavior without changing its implementation.
Context of settings and resources in which work executes.
Transformation of source and dependencies into usable output.
Making a selected software version available in an environment.
Version of software made available to intended consumers.
Produced file or bundle retained for later use or inspection.
Connected systems capable of exchanging data.
Network-layer address identifying a destination or source interface or group, depending on address type.
Transport-layer number distinguishing communication endpoints on a host.
Operating-system communication endpoint used by processes.
Agreed rules for exchanging information.
Connection-oriented transport protocol providing reliable ordered byte delivery.
Distributed naming system that stores and retrieves records associated with domain names.
Hierarchically structured name used by DNS.
Protocol protecting data in transit through confidentiality and integrity, with endpoint authentication as configured.
Application protocol defining requests, responses and their semantics.
HTTP communication secured using TLS.
Identifier specifying a resource location and access scheme.
Participant initiating requests to a service in a client-server interaction.
Participant receiving requests and providing responses or services.
Defined interface through which software components interact.
Address or exposed operation at which a service accepts interaction.
Message asking a server to perform or return something.
Message returned in answer to a request.
Request token specifying the intended operation on the target resource.
Three-digit code describing an HTTP response's semantics, including informational responses, success, redirection and errors.
Named protocol metadata carried with a message.
Content carried by a message, distinguished from protocol framing or metadata.
Intermediary forwarding or handling communication for another participant.
Event-driven HTTP callback to a configured receiver.
Configured limit on how long an operation may wait.
Elapsed time for a particular operation or transmission.
Another attempt at an operation after a prior unsuccessful attempt.
Network-layer protocol family defining packet addressing and delivery across interconnected networks.
Defined sequence or graph of coordinated work.
Event or condition initiating work.
In GitHub Actions, a reusable execution component invoked by a workflow step.
Machine that runs jobs for GitHub Actions; a job can execute in a configured container on that runner.
Group of workflow steps scheduled on a runner; jobs can be ordered by dependencies or run independently.
Individual ordered operation within a workflow job.
Practice of regularly integrating changes and automatically checking them.
Practice of keeping validated changes ready for release; deployment may require approval.
Practice of automatically deploying changes that pass required gates.
Executable or defined check of expected behavior.
Expression or check stating a condition that must hold.
Check focused on a small isolated behavior.
Check of interactions between components.
Check of a complete user or system flow.
Check protecting previously expected behavior from recurrence of a defect.
Small set of checks that a system starts and basic behavior works.
Static check for code patterns, errors or conventions.
Condition that must be satisfied before progression.
Controlled input or environment prepared for a test.
Isolated environment for controlled experimentation.
Traceable observation supporting a claim.
Recorded state permitting verification or resumption.
Property of repeated equivalent operations producing the same intended effect.
Overlapping progress of multiple tasks.
Simultaneous execution of multiple tasks.
Behavior dependent on uncontrolled ordering of concurrent events.
Structure holding work until it can be processed.
Time-limited grant of control over a resource or task.
Periodic signal indicating continued activity or availability.
Defined procedure for restoring an earlier known-good state.
Establishing that an asserted identity is genuine.
Determining whether a subject may perform an operation on a resource.
Evidence used to support identity or access.
Sensitive value whose disclosure could compromise security.
Data representing a security assertion, session or access grant in context.
State associated with a continuing interaction.
Access decisions based on assigned permission-bearing roles.
Limit authority to what is needed for the task.
Transforming data using cryptography to protect confidentiality.
One-way digest function designed for cryptographic security properties.
Cryptographic value used to verify origin and integrity with a public key.
Signed structure binding a public key to identity or other attributes.
Record of security-relevant or accountable actions.
Weakness that can be exploited or triggered to cause harm.
Mechanisms implementing restrictions on resource use.
Recorded information about an occurrence or activity, often with a timestamp and contextual fields.
Numerical measurement collected over time or at a point in time.
Record of a request or operation's path through one or more connected spans.
Representation of a single operation in a trace, typically with a start time, end time and contextual attributes.
Occurrence represented at a particular time.
Notification that a condition requires attention.
A detected problem or invalid condition that may be handled without necessarily ending the operation.
Notice of a condition that may need attention without necessarily stopping work.
Operation met its stated success condition.
An operation's outcome when it does not meet its stated success condition.
Work or decision known to be awaiting progress or a result; unlike unknown, its waiting state is established.
Execution is actively underway.
Work cannot progress until a dependency or constraint is resolved.
Evidence is insufficient to determine the state.
Check or action deliberately not executed.
Execution or planned action was intentionally stopped before normal completion.
Process or service is not currently executing.
Probe of a component's availability or specified readiness.
Whether a component is currently prepared to serve intended work.
Whether a component remains active according to a defined probe.
Classification of impact or urgency according to a defined scale.
Reported condition or outcome at a given time.
